records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: East-west extent. A Pacific-like basin, 60 percent of the real one. At 14.9 km per real minute: 10 hours of pure sailing edge to edge.

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: North-south extent. y = 0 is the north edge, y grows southward.

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Climate latitude at the north and south edges. 150 degrees over 6,000 km = 40 km per degree (real: 111). Compressed 2.8x so every climate belt fits; belts keep their real order and thickness ratios.

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Reference sloop speed on a reach in 14 kn of wind: 5 knots. 222 km per game day = 14.9 km per real minute. Sets every T1 voyage band in km: Hop 45-119, Passage 119-372, Crossing 372-893, Dead Ocean 893-1,786.

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Angle off the wind a sloop cannot sail closer than.

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Wind at which the sloop makes its reference speed.

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Above this the crew reefs; speed stops rising and then falls.

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Significant wave height above which sailing damages the hull.

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Speed lost at 100 percent ice cover.

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Hull wear per game day at full ice cover and full speed, on top of ship.hull_wear_pct_per_day_at_sea.

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Lookout's eye height on deck; horizon = 3.57 x sqrt(h) km = 10 km.

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Visibility of a surface object in clear air (limited by the horizon).

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: visibility = clear x exp(-fog_coeff x fog - rain_coeff x rain).

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: See ocean.fog_vis_coeff.

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: How far region borders wander from straight lines (domain warp amplitude).

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Wavelength of the border warp.

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Regions are zonal (long east-west): north-south distance counts this much more.

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Softness of region borders: environment parameters blend over about twice this distance, so a border takes more than 10 real minutes to cross.

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: One year = 4 seasons of weather.season_length_days. 80 game days = 20 real hours.

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Year phase at game start (0 = northern midwinter, 0.25 = northern spring equinox).

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Typical size of a weather system. At 14.9 km/min a ship needs about 20 real minutes to cross one.

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Time over which a weather system changes shape (45 real minutes).

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Weather systems drift with the prevailing wind at this fraction of its speed.

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: The Herald Swell: a long swell reaches a place this long before the weather that made it. 15 real minutes of warning (fairness, P3).

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Sea surface temperature at the equator.

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Sea surface temperature = equator value - this x latitude squared (28 C at 0, 24 at 30, 19 at 40, 15 at 50, 7 at 60, -1 at 70 before clamping at freezing).

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Sea water freezes here.

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Seasonal swing of the sea surface = this x |latitude|.

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Air temperature is the sea surface plus this, plus a day swing of 1.5 C.

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Significant wave height of a fully developed sea = coeff x wind speed squared (m/s).

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Wave height cap.

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Width of the Rim: the ocean turns you away. Storm and sea ice build over this distance at the world edge, so there is no wall, only weather.

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Icebergs are placed by a hash on a grid of this cell size (deterministic, no state).

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Sun elevation at which regional light reaches zero (civil twilight).

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Sun elevation at which regional light is full.

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Weather is sampled on this grid around the ship and interpolated, never per pixel.

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Only this radius around the ship is simulated or drawn.

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Hard cap on individually simulated animals (Standard profile).

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Cap on fish schools (each is one multimesh, not one object per fish).

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Minimum real time between two naturalist sightings (open water stays calm, no random-encounter spam).

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: Long-term species catalogue target (the owner's brief: more than 200).

records.source: E1 world design; provisional until its owner module
records.note: A region is a place inside a climate belt: every km (north-south) outside its latitude range counts this many km of distance. Keeps polar corners from belonging to temperate regions.
